findings.description: Optional-chain missing on mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration — Reading `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining crashes `EventManager.create` when the entry is absent. Add the `?.` to safely short-circuit.

updateEvent fallback returns undefined calendarId when externalCalendarId missing — The `.find` filter can never match when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the request ships `calendarId: undefined` and fails. Mirror `selectedCalendar`'s fallback to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` via destructuring.

deleteEvent falls back to undefined calendar when externalCalendarId is null — The same broken `.find` in `deleteEvent` forwards `calendarId: undefined` and targets nothing. Destructure `mainHostDestinationCalendar` first and combine with `externalCalendarId`, respecting the existing `defaultCalendarId` guard.

teamDestinationCalendars duplicates accumulate in handleNewBooking — `handleNewBooking` pushes `teamDestinationCalendars` for each member without deduping, so duplicates grow on collective events. Skip insertion when `user.destinationCalendar?.id` already exists in the array.

destinationCalendar falls back to empty instead of user.destinationCalendar — Without a fallback to `bookingToReschedule.user?.destinationCalendar`, reschedule emails and webhook payloads ship `destinationCalendar: []`. Mirror the sibling handlers' pattern before defaulting to an empty array.

Team admin-or-owner check uses && instead of ||, blocking admins — `isTeamAdminOrOwner` wrongly rejects team ADMINs who aren't OWNERs because `&&` reduces the check to OWNER-only. Combine the two predicates with `||` so admins are authorized.

addGuests handler stores newly added guests with an empty name — Newly added guests stored with `name: ""` produce malformed headers like ` <guest@example.com>` in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and drop the attendee name in `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`. Derive a display name from the email's local part instead.

sendAddGuestsEmails uses unfiltered guests instead of uniqueGuests — `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `email-manager.ts` reclassifies existing attendees as new when `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives the un-filtered `guests` list, sending them a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests` so they only get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

addGuestsHandler TOCTOU race on attendee email uniqueness — Two concurrent calls can both pass the filter and insert duplicate attendees since `Attendee` in `schema.prisma` lacks a unique `(bookingId, email)` constraint. Re-read and re-filter inside a `prisma.$transaction` so the check and `createMany` are atomic.

isInvalidEmail persists across retries and re-appears on edit — The inline error stays visible across retries and re-appears alongside an `onError` toast because `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is never cleared. Reset it at the top of `handleAdd` so it reflects only the latest validation.

parseRefreshTokenResponse schema uses computed keys instead of catchall — Computed keys become literal `'ZodString'` rather than a catch-all, so real provider responses with `refresh_token`/`expiry_date` fail validation and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).catchall(z.number())` so arbitrary keys are accepted.

refreshOAuthTokens returns inconsistent shapes across branches — Sync returns a `Response` while no-sync returns `refreshFunction`'s result, and `CalendarService.ts` consumers read `.data`/`.expiresIn` unconditionally, so toggling `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` crashes refresh for those four integrations. Normalize both branches to the same shape before returning.

Race condition in credential findFirst/update/create webhook handler — Two concurrent webhooks for the same `(userId, appSlug)` can both miss the lookup and race to `create`, producing duplicate or failed rows. Replace `findFirst`/`update`/`create` with a single `prisma.credential.upsert` keyed on the unique `(userId, appId)` constraint.

Webhook secret check misses headers due to missing toLowerCase on key — Node lowercases incoming header keys, so a non-lowercase `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` silently breaks verification and effectively disables the webhook. Normalize the lookup key via `.toLowerCase()` before reading `req.headers`.

Pass user id, not credential id, to refreshOAuthTokens — Passing `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` causes the admin sync endpoint to receive the credential row's id as `calcomUserId` and resolve the wrong principal (or reject). Pass `credential.userId` to the third argument of `refreshOAuthTokens`.

Salesforce refresh path returns Connection with stale access_token/instance_url — The returned `jsforce.Connection` still reads `accessToken`/`instanceUrl` from the stale `credentialKey`, so `this.conn` resolves to an expired connection while the DB holds fresh tokens. Pass `accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and `instanceUrl: accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url` when constructing the `Connection`.
Refresh token fallback writes literal "refresh_token" instead of previous token — Set the fallback to `response.refresh_token` or omit the override.

Webhook handler must not 500 on invalid JSON body or decryption failure — `safeParse` and `JSON.parse`/`symmetricDecrypt` throw on bad input and bubble up as Next.js 500s instead of structured errors. Switch to `safeParse` returning `res.status(400).json(...)`, and wrap `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` to return the same 400 on failure.

Webhook secret compared with !== is vulnerable to timing attacks — `!==` short-circuits on length and the first differing byte, letting attackers recover the secret character-by-character via request latency. Compare equal-length `Buffer`s with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.

Non-atomic retryCount increment risks under concurrent cron workers — Concurrent cron workers can both read the same snapshot and overwrite each other's `retryCount` write, leaving retries stuck at 1. Use Prisma's atomic `increment: 1` in both `prisma.workflowReminder.update` calls instead of `reminder.retryCount + 1`.

TOCTOU race in backup-code consumption allows single-use code reuse — The read-modify-write of `backupCodes` is non-atomic, so two concurrent logins both pass `indexOf` before either `prisma.user.update` commits and the same code authenticates twice. Switch to an atomic update conditioned on the prior encrypted value, or store codes individually so DELETE-by-value is atomic.

Unguarded body.backupCodes dereference crashes DisplayBackupCodes render — In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, `handleSetup` calls `body.backupCodes.map` without verifying the field exists, so a malformed response throws inside the catch and leaves the user at an empty `DisplayBackupCodes`. Guard with `Array.isArray(body.backupCodes)` before mapping, or route to the error branch.

raw post.cooked renders unsanitized HTML in embed iframe — Embedding unsanitized `post.cooked` from `Post#cook` allows `<script>` injection (ruby-readability preserves event handlers), so a malicious embeddable_host can run JS in Discourse's origin and steal session cookies. Sanitize raw_html posts through PrettyText or escape here and only unescape known-safe subtrees, using `post.cookedHtml`.

poll_feed loop aborts batch on any per-item error — Any per-item failure in `poll_feed`'s `rss.items.each` loop (e.g. `i.content.scrub` raising `NoMethodError`) drops every remaining item for that hour because `retry: false` swallows the abort. Wrap each iteration in `begin/rescue`, log the exception, and also rescue `Errno::ECONNREFUSED`/`SocketError` around `open()`.
PollFeed runs synchronously inside RetrieveTopic worker — Enqueue it instead via `Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)` so the retriever only schedules the work and returns.

Use URI.open instead of Kernel#open to avoid shell evaluation — Using `Kernel#open` to fetch the feed URL retains shell semantics and executes strings starting with `|`, including any value later typed into `feed_polling_url` in the admin UI. Switch to `URI.open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` so the input is unambiguously treated as a URI.

SQL injection via unsanitized embeddable_hosts interpolation — The `execute` call interpolates `embeddable_hosts` setting values into raw SQL, so any host containing a quote, backslash, or `'),'` either crashes the migration or injects unintended statements. Switch to `sanitize_sql_array` with placeholders so values are bound, not concatenated.

Migration crashes when embed_category site_setting is missing — The first `execute("... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` dereferences `[0]` with no guard, so a missing `embed_category` site_setting raises NoMethodError before the `uncategorized_category_id` fallback runs. Stash the row in a local, check `cmd_tuples > 0`, and default to 0 when absent.

before_validation crashes when host is nil — `before_validation` chains two `self.host.sub!` calls, so a nil `host` raises NoMethodError before `validates_format_of` ever runs. Guard with `return unless host.is_a?(String)` so the callback is a safe no-op when the attribute hasn't been assigned.

Admin::EmbeddingController#update does no persistence, just re-renders — `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` re-renders the `OpenStruct` without persisting, so any PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` returns 200 while changing nothing. Drop the route and the action, or make it perform the work the API expects.

Flex container placed on .contents instead of .row breaks header fallback — In the noscript fallback template, `.title` and `.panel` are inside a regular `.row` block, so `margin-left: auto` and `order: 3` on `.panel` are no-ops and the right alignment breaks. Apply the flex declarations to `.row` instead of `.contents`, or keep `float: right` on `.panel` for non-Ember pages.

Duplicate self.downsize definitions make 4-arg emoji callers fail — Ruby keeps only the last `self.downsize`, so the 5-arg call from `resize_emoji.rb` raises `ArgumentError`. Delete the obsolete 4-arg definition so emoji resize jobs run.

`update` renames group to "" when an empty name param is posted — A blank `params[:name]` is truthy in Ruby, so `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` overwrites the group's name with `""` and fails the 422 on `group.save`. Switch the guard to `params[:name].present?` to match the `alias_level` style on the line above.

add_members drops usernames with surrounding whitespace — `add_members` splits on commas but `User.find_by_username` matches `username_lower`, so a token like `" bob"` returns `nil` and that user is silently dropped while the invite appears to succeed. Trim each token with `username.strip` before the lookup.

remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb for DELETE-only route — The first `.remove_member` example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member` even though the route registers `delete "members"`, masking that the endpoint is DELETE-only and tempting readers to copy the wrong verb. Change the line to `xhr :delete, :remove_member, …` to match the `is able to remove a member` example.

totalPages reports an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit — `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which yields a phantom page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` and pushes `offset` past the data on `next`. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` so the pager only lists pages with content.

FallbackLocaleList#[] mixes String and Symbol, defeating uniq — `Array#uniq` can't deduplicate the mixed `String`/`Symbol` identifiers returned here, so `I18n.ensure_loaded!` parses the same `\.en\.yml$` files and merges into `@translations[:en]` twice on every boot. Normalize with `locale.to_sym` before the `uniq.compact` so each locale loads only once.

Race between device-count check and insert can exceed deviceLimit — Concurrent inserts in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` bypass `deviceLimit` because `CountDevices` and the `INSERT … ON CONFLICT` run as separate statements. Wrap both in a single `WithTransactionalDbSession` at SERIALIZABLE, or push the cap into a conditional `INSERT` that aborts when the count threshold is met.

Cache device key before DB write allows bypass of device limit — `tagDeviceUI` writes to `a.localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs, so a request rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` still authenticates from cache during the TTL. Move `localCache.SetDefault` after a successful DB write (or invalidate the key on error).

Double-checked locking missing second check of cache under exclusive lock — Every goroutine queued behind the exclusive lock performs a redundant read of `assets-manifest.json` and blocks concurrent `RLock()` callers. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` after `Lock()` and return it when non-nil.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48-52`
Async legacy write goroutines inherit request context and short-circuit — Detach them with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying the timeout, so the safety net actually finishes writing.

Storage delete success metric is labeled by object name, inflating cardinality — Labeling the storage histogram with `name` instead of `options.Kind` on the delete success path creates a new Prometheus time series per object, risking Prometheus OOM. Pass `options.Kind` to `d.recordStorageDuration` so the label stays low-cardinality.

Misclassifying storage failure as legacy in DualWriterMode3.Create — A failed storage call is recorded into the legacy histogram, which corrupts the `dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds` metric used by monitoring. Change `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` to `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` so the timing reflects the call that actually failed.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-131`
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:161-167`

BuildIndex drops lock around index creation causing same-key race — Dropping the function-level `b.cacheMu` lock from `BuildIndex` lets two concurrent callers missing the cache both invoke `bleve.New` and `idx.Flush()` on the same disk directory, risking on-disk corruption. Capture the lock, ideally a per-key lock, around the full construction so only one goroutine builds a given key.

NewResourceServer blocks synchronously on Init including search indexing — `NewResourceServer` now synchronously runs `s.Init(ctx)`, which triggers `s.search.init(ctx)` to build all search indexes from `GetResourceStats` before returning. Run `Init` asynchronously (e.g. `go s.Init(s.ctx)`) so every caller—like `pkg/storage/unified/sql/server.go`—no longer blocks on indexing.
AccessTokenContext constructor re-validates grantType instead of rawTokenId — Replace `grantType` with `rawTokenId` in that null check.

AccessTokenContext constructor uses grantType instead of rawTokenId in null check — The blank-check passes `grantType` while its message names `rawTokenId`, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted silently. Pass `rawTokenId` to the `Objects.requireNonNull` argument instead.

isAccessTokenId has inverted and mis-indexed grant-type check — The `isAccessTokenId` matcher in `AssertEvents` uses `substring(3, 5)` and a non-negated equality, so the grant check always passes and every well-formed token matches. Change to `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` to fix the off-by-index and the inversion.

**Also found in:**
- `testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:30-35`
ANCHOR_PATTERN matches any tag starting with 'a', not only anchor tags — Tighten it to `|/>)` so only real ``/`` tokens match.

verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException for English file, bypassing Mojo error handling — A missing English file in `verifySafeHtml` aborts the Maven build with an unhandled stack trace because `verify` only catches `IOException`. Throw `MojoExecutionException` so the failure flows through `ThemeVerifierMojo.execute`'s normal validation channel.

santizeAnchors reports a failure but caller still adds an overlapping illegal-HTML message — When `santizeAnchors` flags an anchor mismatch, `verifySafeHtml` still sanitizes the same string, so each bad key produces two overlapping messages ('Didn't find anchor…' and 'Illegal HTML in key…'). Have `santizeAnchors` signal failure (e.g. return null) so the caller skips the redundant sanitize.

santizeAnchors strips a stale match because the matcher is anchored to the original value — In `santizeAnchors`, the matcher stays bound to the original `value` while `replaceFirst` mutates it, so the substring stripped is no longer the one just visited. Rebuild the matcher each iteration, or collect anchors first and apply them on a fresh pass.
getEvaluationContext is dead code in ClientPermissionsV2 — Remove the method or wire it through an actual V2 token-exchange evaluator before publishing.

registerListener gate uses V1 only, dropping V2-only setups — In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the gate checks only V1's `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`, so V2-only deployments never call `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` on role/client/group removal and orphan permission resources. Match `MgmtPermissions.java:85` by checking `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ || ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2`.

createErrorResponse calls fillContextForm without guarding null/empty authenticators — `fillContextForm` may return early (null) when authenticators are empty, skipping `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED`, `USER_VERIFICATION`, `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS`, and `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` and breaking client-side `initAuthenticate`. Guard the call with a null/empty-authenticators check and populate those attributes directly.

getForLogin misses organization invalidation guard used in getByOrganization — Login cache subsets outlive their organization because `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)` while sibling `getByOrganization` also guards on the org id. Add the `isInvalid(organizationId)` check (and call `cache.invalidateObject` for the affected subset) so removed or updated orgs evict their login IDP entries.

TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty columns, data, meta, and renderer — Every org with `use-table-widget-visualization` sees a blank widget because the new branch hardcodes `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData`. Pass `widget.queries[i]?.fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta` through from the loading-state branch above.

**Also found in:**
- `static/app/views/dashboards/widgetCard/chart.tsx:164-175`
validate_timestamp/validate_age truthiness check treats age=0/timestamp=0 as absent — Replace it with `is not None` so a real zero is still validated.

SpanFlusher silently produces zero workers for non-positive max_processes — A negative `max_processes` produces zero workers because `min(-1, ...)` and `range(-1)` yield empty dicts, so `_create_processes()` is a no-op and backpressure checks silently skip. Guard in `__init__` against `max_processes < 1` and validate `--flusher-processes` via `IntRange(min=1)`.

Avoid redundant Redis cluster memory queries in submit — Each `get_memory_info` call fans out `cluster.info()` across all Redis nodes, so looping `self.buffers.values()` issues N identical cluster-wide queries per submit. Query the cluster once via `next(iter(self.buffers.values())).get_memory_info()` and reuse the result.

AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at class definition — Every `AssignmentSource` instance shares the timestamp captured at class definition, so later `from_integration()` calls see a stale value. Switch `queued` to `field(default_factory=lambda: timezone.now())` so each instance records its own construction time.

OAuthLoginView swallows exceptions only after the network call — `safe_urlopen` in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` runs outside the `try/except`, so a missing `code` or network errors surface as 500s instead of the friendly page. Move the `try` above `safe_urlopen` to mirror `OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token` in oauth2.py.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler will raise TypeError on instantiation — `Detector.detector_handler` (detector.py) catches instantiation in `try/except logger.exception`, so `MetricAlertDetectorHandler`'s new `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` base raises `TypeError` (missing `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`) that's silently swallowed, blocking metric-alert detection. Restore `DetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` or stub the three methods.
